Start a plot: a multilayer network to draw in MiRA

Source: R/mira.R
mira.Rd

Creates a plot of a multilayer network that opens in MiRA, the browser-based multilayer network visualizer. Describe how it should look by adding components with +, as in ggplot2; printing the plot (typing its name at the console) opens it in the browser.

Usage

mira(
  net,
  bipartite = FALSE,
  setA_type = NULL,
  directed = NULL,
  directed_interlayer = NULL
)

Arguments

net

A multilayer object (created by emln::create_multilayer_network() or emln::load_emln()). MiRA does not draw links with weight 0 (weight 0 means "no link" in MiRA); R warns how many there are.

bipartite

Logical. Whether the network is bipartite. Defaults to FALSE. Bipartite is not auto-detected. When TRUE, the nodes table must contain a node_type column (or node_group, or type, as in the networks of load_emln) with exactly two distinct values across the network. MiRA knows the column as node_type, whatever its name in the data.

setA_type

Optional character. The node_type value to render as Set A (top row) in MiRA's bipartite layout. By ecological convention this is the higher trophic level (e.g. "pollinator", "parasite", "disperser"). Only used when bipartite = TRUE.

directed

Logical or NULL. Whether intralayer links are directed. If NULL (default): undirected when bipartite = TRUE (bipartite edge lists usually store each link once, which would look directed); otherwise auto-detected from edge symmetry, as in plot_mira(). R prints which one was chosen.

directed_interlayer

Logical or NULL. Whether interlayer links are directed. If NULL (default), inherits from directed. Interlayer links are directed whenever intralayer links are, so FALSE has no effect on a directed network.

Value

A mira_plot object.

Components

Each component sets one part of the plot. Add them in any order:

  • mira_layout(): where the nodes go (the layout algorithm, a seed).

  • mira_node(): node color, size, shape, labels.

  • mira_intralayer(): the links within layers.

  • mira_interlayer(): the links between layers.

  • mira_layer(): layer colors, names and arrangement.

  • mira_filter(): draw only some nodes, links or layers.

  • mira_camera(): rotate, tilt, zoom and pan the view.

  • mira_legends(): which legends are open, and where.

  • mira_mode_grid(), mira_mode_meta() and the other mira_mode_*(): open the plot in another of MiRA's views (mira_mode).

In each element component, color_by and size_by map an attribute of the data (a column of the network's tables, or one MiRA computes, such as a degree); color, size and shape set constants. The colors of a mapping are chosen in the same component, with color_values, color_scale, color_palette, color_reverse and color_limits: see mira_scales.

Anything not set keeps MiRA's default, and everything can still be changed in MiRA's interface. When the same setting is given twice, the later component wins. A later color replaces an earlier color_by of the same element, and the other way round.

Components are checked against the network as they are added: settings that cannot work (per-set values or the bipartite layout without bipartite = TRUE, a layer name that does not exist) are errors; a column that is not in the network is a warning, and MiRA keeps its default for that setting. mira_spec() shows what a plot sends to MiRA.

MiRA has the final say. When it cannot use a setting it received, it keeps its default for that setting and shows a notice when the plot opens, "Some plot settings from R were ignored", with the reasons; mira_save() gives them as warnings.

Bipartite networks

bipartite = TRUE needs a column in net$nodes that says which of two sets each node is in: node_type, or node_group, or type (what the networks of emln::load_emln() have). MiRA knows it as node_type whatever its name in the data, so mira_node(color_by = "node_type") works for all three. A condition in mira_filter() is evaluated on net$nodes itself and uses the column's own name: type == "bird" for a network from load_emln(). A network made with emln::create_multilayer_network() has no such column; add one before the plot:

# plants: the names of the plant nodes
net$nodes$node_type <- ifelse(net$nodes$node_name %in% plants, "plant", "pollinator")

What MiRA computes

Besides the columns of the data, nodes can be colored and sized by degree and strength, which MiRA computes (mira_node() has the names: intra_degree_sum, ...). mira_options() lists everything a network offers.

See also

mira_spec() to see what a plot sends to MiRA; print.mira_plot() for the browser and port options; plot_mira() to open a network with MiRA's defaults and no components.

Examples

library(emln)
#> 
#> Attaching package: ‘emln’
#> The following object is masked from ‘package:ggmira’:
#> 
#>     plot_multilayer
net <- load_emln(17) # 4 layers; bird and plant nodes
#> Creating state node map
#> Creating extended link list with node IDs

# MiRA's default view
mira(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird")
#> Bipartite network: drawn as undirected. Use directed = TRUE for a directed one.
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# Directed links, within and between layers
mira(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird",
     directed = TRUE, directed_interlayer = TRUE)
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# Add components with +
mira(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird") +
  mira_layout("kamada_kawai", seed = 42) +
  mira_node(color_by = "verification_level", size_by = "intra_degree_sum") +
  mira_intralayer(color_by = "type") +
  mira_interlayer(show = TRUE) +
  mira_layer(labels = TRUE)
#> Bipartite network: drawn as undirected. Use directed = TRUE for a directed one.
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# When done, stop the servers the plots started
httpuv::stopAllServers()
